texts.preamble: State vs . Raghvendra R. on 11 January, 2021 In The Court Of Arvind Bansal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Southeast, Saket Court, New Delhi. State V/s. Raghvendra R. Fir No. 518/2020 Ps. Badarpur U/s. 283 Ipc. Judgment
texts.facts: The case of the prosecution is that on 06.11.2020 at about 5.00 P.M. at IInd 60 Foota Road, Molarband Extension, New Delhi, within the jurisdiction of P.S. Badarpur, which was a public way, accused Raghvendra R. (hereinafter, referred to as "the accused") had stationed his 'rehdi/rehri' on road for selling South Indian Food under the name and style of 'South Indian Masala Dosa' (Ravi Madrasi) and caused obstruction in the public way and thus, committed offence punishable u/s. 283 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter, to be referred as 'IPC'). 2. After investigation, chargesheet was filed on 11.01.2021. The Court took cognizance of offence. Documents were furnished to the accused under section 207 of Criminal Procedure Code, (hereinafter, referred to as Cr.PC). 3. Since the Court was of primafacie view that offence punishable under Sections 283 of IPC was made out against the accused, notice u/s. 251 of Cr.P.C. was served upon the accused for the said offence. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Since the witness was present before the State vs . Raghvendra R. on 11 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79563241/ 1 Court, it proceeded to record evidence in the matter. PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 4. The prosecution examined one witness in support of its case. PW1 HC Santosh Kumar deposed that on 06.11.2020, he was posted as Head Constable at PS Badarpur and on that day, he was on patrolling duty from 05.00 pm to 11.00 pm in the area of Molarband Extension, Badarpur, New Delhi. He further deposed that at about 5.00 pm, while he alongwith Constable Manish was at IInd 60 Foota Road, Molarband Extension, they saw one person, who had stationed his 'rehdi/rehri' on road for selling South Indian Food under the name and style of 'South Indian Masala Dosa' (Ravi Madarasi). Due to this act, the commuters / passerby were having obstruction in their movement. He clicked the photographs of the shop, which are MarkP (Colly.). Further, he deposed that he prepared tehrir, which is Ex.PW1/A under his signatures and handed over the same to Ct. Manish for getting the FIR registered. Thereafter, Ct. Manish got the FIR registered from the PS and returned with the copy of FIR along with original tehrir and handed over the same to the witness. He further deposed that the accused was arrested at the spot vide arrest memo Ex. PW1/B, which bears his signature at point A. Accused was released on police bail. The site plan was prepared at the spot by him and the same is Ex.PW1/C, bearing his signature at point 'A'. Witness was duly cross examined. 5. Vide a separate statement, accused admitted the genuineness of following document (without admitting the contents thereof): (a). FIR No. 518/2020, PS Badarpur with certificate u/s.65B of Indian Evidence Act as Ex. A1 (Colly.). 6. Prosecution evidence was closed and statement of accused u/s. 313 Cr.P.C read with Section 281 Cr.P.C was recorded, wherein he denied the incriminating evidence against him. He stated that he did not wish to lead defence evidence.
texts.arguments: To bring home the guilt of the accused under section 283 IPC, the prosecution is required to establish the following essential ingredients beyond reasonable doubt: (i) that the accused did an act or ommitted to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge. (ii) that such act or omission caused danger / obstruction / injury to any person in any public way or line of navigation. In Latesh @ Dadu Babu Rao Karlekar vs. State of Maharashtra (2018) 3SCC 66 "reasonable doubt" has been enunciated by Hon'ble Apex Court as a mean between excessive caution and excessive indifference to a doubt. Reliance is placed upon Anand Ramachandra Chougala Vs. Sidarai Laxman Chougala & Ors. (Crl. Appl. No.1006/2010) and State of Karnataka Vs. Sidarai Laxman Chougala & Ors. (Crl. Appeal No. 1007/2010) decided by the Apex Court on 06.08.2019. 10. Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case titled 'Nand Ram Vs. Sub Divisional Judge, 1969 Crl.L.J. 77 (DELHI)'observed as follows: "the plain reading of the Section would show that the real gravamen of the offence lies in the accused acting or ommitting to take order with any property in his possession or under his charge and thereby causing danger, obstruction or injury to any person in public way, etc."
